text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet agrees in principle the terms of the new five-year project and new budget -- no new burdens or new duties on citizens. Subsidies to continue on basic and strategic goods.
- Mubarak sends message to Arafat. Dennis Ross to visit region next week. Palestinian delegation in Washington to discuss U.S. ideas on ways to save peace process.
- Mubarak to address new local councils during their first meeting next Tuesday.
- Egyptian-Indian committee signs six agreements on investment, tourism and education.
- Health minister says there will be a unified price for medicines.
- Ganzouri to head meeting of ministers' council for privatisation to discuss sale of new group of public sector companies.
- Presidential adviser Osama el-Baz says Arab and Egyptian position surprised Israel.
- Clinton says there is still a chance the peace process can be resumed.
- Tourism minister orders closure of companies that issued forged pilgrimage visas.
